clue.text: There's nothing in between the passenger and the road

indicators.note: the nothing sits inside the word for between, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
a word meaning by way of, from one side to the other
a fare is a paying passenger in a taxi

explanation.surface: A remark that nothing separates the traveller from the tarmac, as in a car with a hole in the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between' looks like a positional word, but here it is a synonym, and the nothing goes inside it near the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a public street or main route that traffic passes along.

clue.text: Recluse carries tons of welding material

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tons
a hermit lives alone, away from society

explanation.surface: A loner hauling heavy loads of stuff for a welding job.
explanation.walkthrough: The recluse carries the T at its front, so T simply leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermit is a mixture of aluminium powder and iron oxide that burns hot enough to fuse rail joints.

clue.text: Herb loves holding Shakespearean

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it in your grasp, so the loves enclose the character

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O; two of them here
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A herb that adores Shakespeare, a whimsical garden picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic culinary plant of the mint family, used in Mediterranean cooking.

clue.text: Expenditure one invested in unfashionable medals

indicators.note: money invested in a venture is put inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: something out of fashion is out
gongs is British slang for medals or honours
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Spending money by putting it into old-fashioned decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: Gongs is British slang for medals or honours; the one goes in after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings are the regular sums of money a person or business pays out.

clue.text: Boss endlessly making faux pas

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word for boss is removed

blocks.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: A boss who keeps on putting their foot in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter of GAFFER to leave GAFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder, exactly what the French phrase for a false step describes.

clue.text: Supply swimmer taking pot

indicators.note: the swimmer takes the pot into itself, so the pot ends up inside

blocks.note: a fish swims
an urn is a large pot or vase

explanation.surface: A supplier of swimmers grabbing a pot, perhaps a pool stocking trophies.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish is to provide or equip someone with what they need.

clue.text: Composer's baton Igor smashed

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into bits that can be put back in a new order

blocks.note: a baton is a short rod
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conductor's stick broken by a man called Igor, as if Stravinsky lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Joaquin Rodrigo was the Spanish composer of the Concierto de Aranjuez for guitar.

clue.text: Proper sauce for traditional festivity

blocks.note: done properly is done well
a dressing is a sauce for salad

explanation.surface: The right sauce to serve at a traditional celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Well dressing is a Derbyshire custom of decorating village wells with pictures made from flower petals.
explanation.definitionFit: Well dressing is an old English village celebration, held each summer around the decorated wells.

clue.text: Woman gets support for surveyor

blocks.note: Eve, the first woman
a rest is a support, as for a snooker cue

explanation.surface: A woman receives backing for a land surveyor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a person: Sir George Everest, after whom the mountain is named.
explanation.definitionFit: George Everest was Surveyor General of India, and the peak was named in his honour.

clue.text: I forged alloy in the hearth

definitions.note: describes where the answer is found, not the noun itself

indicators.note: an alloy is a mixture of metals, so the letters are mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A smith boasting of making metal at the fireside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forged' looks like the shuffle signal, but it is fodder; 'alloy' means mix, and the definition is the fireside location.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog is an andiron, one of a pair of metal supports holding logs in an open fireplace.

clue.text: Officers rent shop

blocks.note: generals are senior army officers
rent as the past tense of rend, to tear

explanation.surface: Military officers paying rent on a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' reads as payment but is the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A general store is a shop, typically rural, selling a wide range of goods.

clue.text: Business graduate in drag faces old complaint

indicators.note: the graduate is placed inside the word for drag

blocks.note: to lug is to drag something heavy
Master of Business Administration
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An MBA in drag confronting an old grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In drag' suggests cross-dressing; drag is the verb lug.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back, a medical complaint or ailment.

clue.text: Subversion lacks its initial impression

indicators.note: the word for subversion goes without its first letter

blocks.note: sedition is conduct inciting rebellion against authority

explanation.surface: Subversive activity that has lost its opening impact.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, an impression is one print run of a book, much like an edition.

clue.text: The proportion of a square in a South American city

indicators.note: the a and the square are placed inside the name of the city

blocks.note: taken as written
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T
Rio de Janeiro in Brazil

explanation.surface: How much of a city like Rio is taken up by a plaza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' suggests a plaza, but it stands for T, from the T-square.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the relation in quantity of one thing to another, expressed as a proportion.

clue.text: Make a beastly noise before our local resident

blocks.note: a horse neighs
B stands for before, as in BC
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone braying loudly in front of the nearby householder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' reads as a placing word, but it must also give its abbreviation B, as in BC.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour lives next door or nearby, a resident of the same locality.

clue.text: Fast runner tucks into rice cooked for northerner

indicators.note: to tuck into is to get inside, so the runner goes within the other letters
cooking changes ingredients, so the letters of rice are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
an eland is a fast African antelope

explanation.surface: A sprinter digging into a plate of cooked rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucks into' suggests eating; here it puts the antelope inside the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelander comes from Iceland, a nation in the far north Atlantic.

clue.text: Susie dies foolishly for a matter of lesser importance

indicators.note: acting foolishly means behaving in a muddled way, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Susie's silly death turns out to be beside the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a secondary concern, peripheral to the main question under discussion.

clue.text: Tory supports change in capital of a Greek island

indicators.note: the change is placed inside the word for capital
in a down clue a support holds up from below, so the Tory comes last

blocks.note: Delhi, capital of India
p for penny, small change
C for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Conservative backing reform in the main town of an Aegean island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the supporter sits below, so C comes last. Delphi, home of the oracle, is in fact on the Greek mainland, so the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphic means relating to Delphi and its oracle, an ancient Greek sanctuary site.

clue.text: Engineer breaking local's key? Holy smoke!

indicators.note: breaking into something splits it open, so the engineer goes inside the other word

blocks.note: a local is a pub, an inn; the 's adds S
CE is Civil Engineer
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An engineer smashing the pub's lock, met with a startled exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy smoke!' looks like an exclamation of surprise but literally describes the answer. A local is British slang for one's regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Incense is burned in religious ceremonies, giving sacred fragrant fumes.

clue.text: Merchandise keeps wife smart

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so the wife is held inside the other word

blocks.note: to merchandise goods is to sell them
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Shopping keeps a wife well turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merchandise' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Swell as an adjective means stylish or fashionable, especially in older informal usage.

clue.text: Life cut short in travesty of transportation

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter of life goes
the shortened word is placed inside the word for travesty

blocks.note: a skit is a parody or travesty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A life sentence cut short through a farcical deportation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transportation' suggests penal exile to a colony; here it is literally a means of carrying people up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski-lift is a cable system carrying skiers up the mountain, a form of conveyance.

clue.text: German aristocrat is English reader

blocks.note: E for English
a lector reads lessons in church or lectures in a university

explanation.surface: A German nobleman turns out to be an English reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Electors were German princes entitled to choose the Holy Roman Emperor.

clue.text: Wrongfully in charge? It's criminal

blocks.note: ill as an adverb, badly or wrongly
IC is the abbreviation for in charge
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly put in charge, which is criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law, unlawful, just as a criminal act is.

clue.text: Wrench Bob away to keep fit

indicators.note: the bob is sent away, so that letter is removed from the word for wrench

blocks.note: to wrench a muscle is to strain it
a bob is an old British shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: Pulling Bob aside to help him stay in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a man's name; it is old slang for a shilling, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to exercise regularly to stay in good physical condition.

clue.text: Insect eats fruit for food

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside, so the fruit ends up within the insect

blocks.note: an ant is an insect
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A bug feeding on fruit as its meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment or sustenance.

clue.text: Goddess gets shrub in a place of torment

blocks.note: Ge, or Gaia, the Greek earth goddess
henna is a shrub whose leaves give a reddish dye

explanation.surface: A goddess is given a bush in a hellish spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Gehenna is a biblical name for hell, where the wicked suffer after death.

clue.text: Disagreement in the German fishing boat

indicators.note: the disagreement is placed inside the German article

blocks.note: der is a German word for the
a rift is a split or quarrel

explanation.surface: A quarrel aboard a German trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a boat that fishes with drift nets left to float with the tide.

clue.text: One puts words into the mouths of those to be shot

definitions.text: One puts words into the mouths of those to be shot

blocks.note: surface reading: people facing a firing squad, given last words

blocks.clueFragment: One puts words into the mouths
blocks.note: setter's reading: someone who writes dialogue for actors who will be filmed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests execution, but in film-making actors are shot by the camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenwriter writes the scripts, scenes and lines spoken by performers in films.
